full_name: Two-Phase Randomized Stochastic Mirror Descent (2-RSMD) for Nonconvex Stochastic Composite Optimization
source_reference: Lan, First-order and Stochastic Optimization Methods for Machine Learning, Springer 2020 (Theorem 6.7)

problem.description: Nonconvex stochastic composite optimization over a closed convex set

variable_space.math: X \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n \text{ closed convex}; \; f : X \to \mathbb{R} \text{ continuously differentiable, possibly nonconvex}; \; h : X \to \mathbb{R} \text{ simple convex, possibly nonsmooth}

assumptions.name: L-smoothness
assumptions.math: \|\nabla f(y) - \nabla f(x)\| \le L \|y - x\|, \quad \forall x, y \in X

assumptions.name: Euclidean norm
assumptions.math: \|\cdot\| \text{ is associated with the inner product } \langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle; \text{ Section 6.2.3.2 assumes the standard Euclidean norm}

initialization.math: x_1 \in X, \; S \text{ (number of runs)}, \; \bar{N} \text{ (total SFO calls per run)}, \; T \text{ (post-optimization sample size)}

steps.name: Optimization phase (S independent RSMD runs)
steps.math: \text{For } s = 1, \ldots, S: \text{ call the RSMD algorithm with } N = \lfloor \bar{N}/m \rfloor, \; \gamma_k = 1/(2L), \; m_k = m, \; P_R \text{ as (6.2.30)}. \; \text{Let } \bar{x}_s = x_{R_s}.

steps.name: RSMD inner update (mini-batch mirror descent)
steps.math: G_k = \frac{1}{m_k} \sum_{i=1}^{m_k} G(x_k, \xi_{k,i}), \quad x_{k+1} = \operatorname{argmin}_{u \in X} \left\{ \langle G_k, u \rangle + \frac{1}{\gamma_k} V(x_k, u) + h(u) \right\}

steps.name: Post-optimization phase (selection by empirical projected gradient)

parameters.name: P_X
parameters.math: P_X(x, g, \gamma) = \frac{1}{\gamma}(x - x^+), \quad x^+ = \operatorname{argmin}_{u \in X} \left\{ \langle g, u \rangle + \frac{1}{\gamma} V(x, u) + h(u) \right\}

main_theorem.statement_math: \text{(a) Let } \mathscr{B}_{\bar{N}} \text{ be defined in (6.2.47). Then, for all } \lambda > 0, \quad \operatorname{Prob}\left\{ \|g_X(\bar{x}^*)\|^2 \ge 2\left(4L \mathscr{B}_{\bar{N}} + \frac{3\lambda \sigma^2}{T}\right) \right\} \le \frac{S}{\lambda} + 2^{-S}. \quad \text{(b) Let } \epsilon > 0, \; \Lambda \in (0,1). \text{ Set } S(\Lambda) = \lceil \log_2(2/\Lambda) \rceil, \; \bar{N}(\epsilon) = \left\lceil \max\left\{ \frac{512 L^2 D_\Psi^2}{\epsilon}, \left[\left(\tilde{D} + \frac{D_\Psi^2}{\tilde{D}}\right) \frac{128\sqrt{6} L \sigma}{\epsilon}\right]^2, \frac{3\sigma^2}{8L^2 \tilde{D}^2} \right\} \right\rceil, \; T(\epsilon, \Lambda) = \left\lceil \frac{24 S(\Lambda) \sigma^2}{\Lambda \epsilon} \right\rceil. \text{ Then 2-RSMD computes an } (\epsilon, \Lambda)\text{-solution after at most } S(\Lambda)[\bar{N}(\epsilon) + T(\epsilon, \Lambda)] \text{ SFO calls.}

proof.description: Apply the deterministic norm decomposition to the selected candidate: split the true projected gradient into optimization error (min over runs) and post-optimization estimation error (max over runs)
Bound the optimization term using independence of the S runs and the one-run Markov tail bound with lambda=2
Bound the post-optimization estimation error using Proposition 6.1, Lemma 6.1(a), and a union bound over all S candidates
Combine steps 1-3 to obtain the tail probability bound (6.2.56)
Substitute the parameter choices S(Lambda), N_bar(epsilon), T(epsilon,Lambda) and verify that the resulting bound yields an (epsilon,Lambda)-solution with the stated oracle complexity

key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{For any } g_1, g_2 \in \mathbb{R}^n, \quad \|P_X(x, g_1, \gamma) - P_X(x, g_2, \gamma)\| \le \|g_1 - g_2\|

key_lemmas.role: Provides the fundamental expected stationarity bound for a single RSMD run with general stepsizes and batch sizes

proof.description: Use smoothness (6.2.3), the RSMD update (6.2.29), and the definition of the stochastic projected gradient to derive the one-step recursion

key_lemmas.name: Constant-step RSMD specialization (Corollary 6.6)

key_lemmas.name: Budgeted RSMD bound (Corollary 6.7)
key_lemmas.role: Converts the per-iteration bound into a total-SFO-budget bound by balancing batch size against iteration count

proof.description: Use the total-budget relation N >= N_bar/(2m) together with (6.2.44) to write the error as a sum of a term proportional to m/N_bar and a term proportional to 1/m
